messages:
maya: quick pulse check — after the kernel swap last night we're seeing regional prefix hit disparities in ap-south, up ~8% miss compared to eu-west.  anyone digging into routing or replication windows?
sam: saw the graphs, thanks. initial hunch: kernel selection changed batching behaviour which increases short-tail latency and reduces effective cache reuse for small prefixes. will profile.
leo: fwiw ap-south traffic is burstier (mobile app), so small prefixes dominate. kernel change altered micro-batching thresholds so many requests missed the batch window and fell through to cold KV paths.
anya: adding to that — replication lag metrics show a subtle tail at commit-coalesce step around 17-18s for ap-south replicas. could be causing stale reads after failover and lowering observed hit-rate.
maya: ok two axes: (1) kernel batching thresholds changed, (2) replication/coherency tail. can we get a quick perf profile + KV access trace for a sample 10k reqs from ap-south between 02:00-03:00 UTC?
sam: running a quick flame and kv-op summary now. attaching short summary when ready. perf-bot: started trace job job-id=trace-2087-ap-south-02
perf-bot: job complete — /s3/redwood/traces/trace-2087-ap-south-02/profile.json (12MB)
leo: skimmed the flame: kernel now prefers int8-quantized matmul kernels for sequence <=128 which reduced per-token cost but added ~0.6ms jitter to first-token due to extra code-path selection. that jitter pushes micro-batcher timeout.
anya: kv traces: saw a spike of `kv_miss -> remote_fetch` transitions clustered around 02:18:15 with an increased remote_fetch latency median from 2.1ms -> 5.7ms. replication commit_coalesce seemed to pause flush for ~15s windows.
maya: can we simulate the batching effect by toggling micro-batch timeout from 4ms to 2ms in a canary? i'd prefer reducing batching timeout so small prefixes get aggregated more predictably even if that slightly ups per-token CPU.
sam: yes. I can push a runtime flag `micro_batch_ms=2` to canary pool cpusrv-16 in ap-south. will run 30m smoke.
leo: alternatively we can gate kernel selection to prefer the old stable matmul for <64 tokens in ap-south region with `kernel_hint=legacy_small`. that avoids the jitter while keeping quantized path for long sequences.
anya: replication side — we should lower commit_coalesce window from 20s -> 5s for ap-south or enable opportunistic async-ack to reduce stale-read window. tradeoff: slightly more RF write amplification.
maya: prefer minimizing user-visible misses first. plan: (A) canary micro_batch_ms=2 immediate; (B) run kernel gate A/B for small seqs; (C) monitor kv hit-rate, cold-miss tail, and P99 latency. sam can you do A? leo do B? anya do C and replication tweak if A/B don't help.
sam: on it. pushing flag to cpusrv-16 canary now.`kubectl apply -f -` snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: runtime-config-canary
data:
  micro_batch_ms: "2"
```
sam: canary applied 02:32 UTC. starting 30m run.
leo: preparing kernel gate patch, will flip on canary using feature-flag `kernel_gate_smallseq` (rollout 10% -> 50%)
anya: replication tweak in a separate canary: lowering commit_coalesce to 5s on replica set rr-ap-south-2. will observe write amplification metric `kv_write_bytes_total`.
maya: good. also add a synthetic warmup: run prefix primer for top-2000 prefixes from last 24h via regional prefetch job to pre-warm KV cache. this should help cold tails while we iterate.
sam: canary metrics 15m in: micro-batch aggregation increased by 27% for <=64 token requests, first-token latency p50 down 0.9ms, p95 down 1.8ms. kv miss rate improved from 12.4% -> 9.2% in canary.
leo: kernel gate A/B preliminary: 10% traffic saved the jitter. smallseq flows when on legacy kernel show consistent ~0.6ms less tail.
anya: replication tweak: commit_coalesce=5s reduced stale-read windows but increased `kv_write_bytes_total` by 3.4% (expected). downstream replayer shows cold-miss reduction ~1.5%.
maya: nice. does combined A+B+C meet our target? target was reduce regional miss gap to <=2% vs eu-west and keep p99 latency budget.
sam: combined stats from canary pool: regional miss gap reduced to 1.7%, p99 latency within SLO (ap-south p99 130ms, SLO 150ms). CPU cost uptick marginal (+2.1%).
leo: will prepare rollout plan: kernel_gate_smallseq -> 50% over 1h, micro_batch_ms=2 -> apply to all ap-south serving nodes in 2h, replication_coalesce->5s -> keep for 24h and monitor.
anya: note: need to ensure prefetch primer doesn't bias evals. we'll tag primer traffic with header `x-primer:1` and exclude from client-metrics.
maya: good call. also add an automated regression test: run synthetic workload that mirrors mobile small-prefix distribution and assert cache-hit >= 90% and p99 <150ms. put in perf infra.
sam: I'll add the canary dashboards and an alert `ap-south-prefix-hit-gap` if gap >3% for 15m.
leo: one more observation from traces: KV key normalization trimmed trailing whitespace differently between old/new kernel path which caused some evictions. adding a normalization hook in the runtime to canonicalize keys should reduce accidental misses.
anya: yes — simple canonicalization: `s/\s+/ /g; trim()` before hashing. can roll as a low-risk patch.
maya: timeline: immediate - keep canary flags for 2h, medium - roll kernel gate to 50% and micro_batch_ms across region in next 6h if stable, long - consider making kernel selection adaptive by region/traffic pattern. thanks team.
sam: thanks, will post canary links and dashboards here in 10m :thumbsup:
perf-bot: canary-dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/trace-2087-ap-south
maya: closing loop — we'll re-evaluate tomorrow morning after 24h metrics. :rocket:
